diagnostic_evidence.quote:
if $T\subset K\subset\R^d$ are convex bodies and $T$ is symmetric ($T=-T$), then for all $h>0$,
\[\mc{N}(K,hT)\leq (1+2h^{-1})^d\mc{N}(K,T).\]

issues.failure_explanation: The invoked result is stated only for $T\subset K$, but the lemma assumes no containment $V_0\subset B_R$. Thus the displayed conclusion does not follow from the cited fact in the parameter range stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard submultiplicativity argument covering each translate of $V_0$ by translates of $hV_0$, or add and consistently enforce a containment condition after enlarging $R$.
issues.overall_effect: The covering estimate used to obtain finite-term approximation bounds lacks a valid proof for arbitrary $R$.
issues.title: Covering-number estimate is applied without its stated containment hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A short standard covering-number argument can restore the same estimate and all downstream rates without changing the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The lower bound in EQN:xbound yields $|x|^p\geq ||h\lambda|-\rad(V_{h\lambda})|^p$, not $|x|^p\geq ||h\lambda|^p-\rad(V_{h\lambda})^p|$. The latter is false for $p>1$. For example, in one dimension with $\Lambda=\mathbb Z$, $h=1$, $p=2$, and a Dirac mass at $x=1/2+\eta$ assigned to the cell centered at 1, the claimed estimate becomes $1\leq1/4+(1/2+\eta)^2$, which fails for small positive $\eta$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace part (i) by the routine estimate obtained from $|h\lambda|\leq |x|+h\rad(V_0)$, with the necessary $2^{p-1}$ factors, and propagate that harmless change through the moment calculations.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's stated moment estimate is false, and both main infinite-lattice theorems invoke it to establish that their approximants have finite p-th moment.
issues.title: The first radial estimate is false for general p
issues.why_classification: The false auxiliary constant is repaired by a local elementary inequality; finiteness and all advertised Wasserstein error bounds remain unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given two convex bodies $K$ and $T$, let $\mc{N}(K,T)$ be the minimal number of translates of $T$ it takes to cover $K$

issues.failure_explanation: The number of nonzero coefficients is the number of cells in the fixed Voronoi tiling that receive mass. The minimum number of arbitrarily translated copies of $hV_0$ covering $B_R$ does not, by definition, upper-bound that fixed-cell count. Moreover, the chosen $h$ need not lie in $(0,1]$, although both cited estimates are stated only in that range.

failure_location.quote:
Note that for any $h\in(0,1]$, $\mu_h$ has at most \[\mc{N}(B_R,hV_{0}) \leq 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}(B_R,V_0) = 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}\]
terms

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a separate lattice-cell counting estimate for cells intersecting $B_R$, adjust the scaling constant if necessary, and handle the regime where the selected $h>1$ or extend the preceding results to all $h>0$.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed at-most-$N$ support guarantee and the finite-term deductions based on it are not established, even though the Wasserstein error estimate for the full lattice remains available.
issues.title: A minimum covering number does not count occupied fixed lattice cells
issues.why_classification: Restoring the finite-term guarantee requires a genuine geometric counting argument and potentially a rescaling, rather than a routine algebraic edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.failure_explanation: The centered infinite lattice does not generally partition the unit cube into exactly $N$ Voronoi cells. Already for $d=1$ and even $N$, the interval $(-1/2,1/2)$ intersects the $N+1$ cells centered at $k/N$ for $k=-N/2,\ldots,N/2$. A compactly supported measure assigning positive mass inside each such intersection makes the displayed approximant have $N+1$ terms. In higher dimensions, arbitrary $N$ need not even be a perfect $d$th power.

failure_location.quote: Then $\mu_N = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_N}\mu(V_{\lambda})\delta_{\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation to $\mu$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Align or translate a finite grid with the cube and restrict the grid dimensions appropriately, or choose an integer grid resolution such as $\lfloor N^{1/d}\rfloor$ and adjust the error constant.
issues.overall_effect: The Wasserstein bound follows cellwise, but the asserted at-most-$N$ complexity guarantee is false for the stated lattice and arbitrary $N$.
issues.title: The pixel-grid construction can use more than N lattice points
issues.why_classification: A comparable rate survives, but the construction and parameterization must be changed to recover the exact term budget for all $N$.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, $\one_{h\lambda}$ and $\one_\lambda$ are indicators of singleton points. Interpreted as Lebesgue densities, they integrate to zero, so the displayed objects are not probability measures and cannot satisfy the asserted Wasserstein guarantees. COR:NpixelIndicator also uses the undefined quantity $|V_{h\lambda}|$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every singleton indicator by the corresponding cell indicator $\one_{V_{h\lambda}}$ or $\one_{V_\lambda}$ and, in COR:NpixelIndicator, replace the undefined denominator by $|V_\lambda|$.
issues.overall_effect: All finite piecewise-constant corollaries display the wrong approximating measure, making their stated constructions and guarantees invalid as written.
issues.title: Finite piecewise-constant approximants use indicators of points
issues.why_classification: The intended cellwise densities are unambiguous from the preceding theorem, and local notation corrections restore the constructions without changing the argument or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Mimic the proof of Theorem \ref{THM:NTermDirac} \textit{mutatis mudandis}

issues.failure_explanation: The needed quantity is $\mc N(B_R,V_0)$, which covers the support ball by Voronoi-cell translates. The stated $\mc N(V_0,B_R)$ covers the cell by balls and gives no control on how many scaled cells can meet the support. For large $R$, it can equal 1 while the number of occupied cells grows with $R^d$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\mc N(V_0,B_R)$ consistently by $\mc N(B_R,V_0)$ and then supply the fixed-cell counting argument required by THM:NTermDirac.
issues.overall_effect: Even after correcting the displayed density, the stated choice of $h$ does not ensure an $N$-term approximation or the claimed constant.
issues.title: The piecewise N-term corollary reverses the covering-number arguments
issues.why_classification: Reversing the arguments is a local correction, although the shared counting gap must separately be repaired.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $f_\mu(x) \leq \frac{\eps^p}{ 3C \vert x \vert^{p+d+1} }$ where $C$ is the integration constant from integrating over concentric $d$-spheres

issues.failure_explanation: The radial integral is $\int_R^\infty r^{-2}\,dr=1/R$, not a quantity bounded by 1 for arbitrary $R$. Since the theorem imposes no condition $R\geq1$, assumption (1) does not imply $I_1\leq\eps^p/3$ when $R<1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require $R\geq1$, or strengthen the density constant by the missing factor depending on $R$ and repeat the radial calculation.
issues.overall_effect: The truncation error bound can fail for admissible small radii, invalidating the theorem and its final approximation corollary in that regime.
issues.title: The absolutely continuous tail estimate fails when R is small
issues.why_classification: A local radius restriction or constant adjustment repairs this component without changing the decay order or approximation architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: If $R$ is not an integer, the first denominator is $\lfloor R\rfloor+1-R\in(0,1)$, so the first summand alone exceeds 1 and the whole series need not be at most $\pi^2/6$. For $R$ close to the next integer it becomes arbitrarily large. Consequently assumption (2) does not yield $I_2\leq\eps^p/3$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Index shells from the radius itself, for example $B_{(R+n,R+n+1]}$, and impose a decay bound normalized by $(n+1)^{p+2}$, or alter the normalization constant to account for the fractional part of $R$.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's truncation guarantee is unsupported for singular-continuous mass whenever the radius is nonintegral, and the downstream approximation bound inherits the failure.
issues.title: The singular-continuous shell summation uses a false series bound
issues.why_classification: Reindexing the annuli and their decay condition is a contained local repair preserving the same tail exponent and final guarantee.
